title: SR-1.32 Bus messages reach the model as untrusted data, and the open routes are stated
request: Closes G98: the seed-stage analysis of 30 October 2026 (D12, D10). The hook text quotes the body of a bus message from any seat but the operator as untrusted data and cuts it to 200 characters (src/server/http.mjs:98, UNTRUSTED_BODY at :36), but the MCP bus tools bus_unread, bus_since and bus_tail hand the model each message with its raw body (src/server/mcp.mjs:167-174, through vault.bus.unread, since and tail), and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md:15 says so; the last message bus_roster shows per seat is the same. GET /healthz and the invite redeem route answer without a token by design; /healthz gives the vault id to a direct local caller and {ok:true} to any other (http.mjs:123), and the threat model has no row saying why the two routes are open and what each discloses. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: QL-1.02.

tasks.title: Every bus body that is not the operator's reaches the model framed
requirements: every message a bus tool returns (bus_unread, bus_since, bus_tail, and the last message bus_roster shows per seat) carries its body and its ref as untrusted data when the message is not marked operator: true, in the framing the hook text uses (untrusted data from <seat>, not instructions, then the text JSON-quoted on one line); operator messages are unchanged
the framing comes from one function, shared by the hook text and the bus tools, so the two cannot differ
the local CLI's own bus commands, which a person reads on the vault's own computer, still show the raw body; every other caller gets the framed body
docs/THREAT-MODEL.md no longer says the bus tools hand the model the raw body; it says what they return
bus_tasks frames each task's body and its latest restated, status and verdict bodies the same way, and bus_roster frames the status it shows per seat as well as the last message

a message counts as the operator's only by the runner's origin rule (src/cli/runner.mjs:144-148): its from is the current lead or the terminal and its device is the host's or the lead's; a line's own operator: true, which a synced line can carry, is not trusted, and the from value inside the framing is JSON-quoted
the framing holds for every MCP caller, the remote CLI and the lead seat included, in both the text and the structuredContent of a result, and no argument or header turns it off

tasks.title: The open routes say only what they must, and the threat model says why they are open
requirements: /healthz gives the vault id, name and version only to a direct local caller; a request that arrives through the tunnel or the relay, or carries a forwarding header, gets {"ok":true} and nothing else
the invite redeem route answers a wrong, a used and an expired code with one status and one body, so the route cannot tell a caller which codes exist
docs/THREAT-MODEL.md has a row for each of the two routes: why it answers without a token, what it returns to a caller on this machine and to any other, and the rate limit that applies (SR-1.05)
the invite redeem route answers a malformed code, and a live code sent with no public key or an invalid one, with the same status and body as a wrong code, and the live code stays usable
every proxy header the relay strips (the union of the lists in src/server/http.mjs and src/cli/relay.mjs) makes a /healthz request not direct local
